q: What is the total energy use and CO2 of the Ballari iron and steel cluster outside the integrated plant?
title: Ballari steel cluster: energy and CO2
short: Leaving out JSW's integrated plant, TERI's 2025 study counts 42 iron and steel plants in Ballari making 8.71 million t a year, using 1.84 Mtoe and emitting 8.34 million t CO2. Sponge iron is most of it: 27 plants and 5.64 million t CO2, about two thirds.
audience: Sponge iron, pellet, induction furnace, re-rolling and ferro alloy plants in Ballari district, Karnataka

ul: Sponge iron: 27 (23 stand-alone, 4 within composite plants), 2.616 million t.
Pellets: 4, 4.54 million t. Induction furnace: 3. Re-rolling: 4. Ferro alloy: 2. One mini blast furnace and one BF-BOF plant.
Most are designated consumers under BEE's PAT scheme, so they already report energy to BEE.

p: Coal and coke, 3.34 million t a year, give 94% of the energy and 7.4 million t CO2, more than 88% of the total. Sponge iron kilns burn 2.61 million t of it. Electricity, 1,330 million kWh, is 6% of energy and about 11% of CO2.

sections.h: Why a cluster average per tonne misleads
p: 8.34 / 8.71 looks like 0.96 t CO2 a tonne, but more than half of the 8.71 million t is pellets that go on into the kilns, so tonnes are counted twice. Use the figure for your own process instead.

ul: Sponge iron: waste heat power, kiln preheating from waste heat, pellets in place of lump ore, mullite kiln lining, drives on fans and pumps, and in time gas-based DRI.
Induction furnaces: scrap bundling, continuous casting with direct rolling.
Re-rolling: recuperators, coal gasifiers in place of pulverised coal, better furnace lining.

example.title: CO2 per tonne by process (from the study)
lines: Sponge iron: 5.64 million t / 2.616 million t = 2.16 t CO2 per tonne
Ferro alloy: 0.60 / 0.137 = 4.4 t CO2 per tonne
Mini blast furnace: 0.49 / 0.24 = 2.0 t CO2 per tonne
Induction furnace: 0.21 / 0.30 = 0.70 t CO2 per tonne
example.note: Production and CO2 from TERI's 2025 Ballari study, which excludes JSW's integrated plant.

senseible: Senseible reads coal invoices (1.76 t CO2 a tonne Indian, 2.44 imported) and power bills into monthly records; electricity stays in the record for buyers' footprints even though CBAM leaves it out for steel. It has no built-in coke factor.
